security_awareness.title: Safe security awareness exercise
security_awareness.content: Run simulations only with written approval, a defined audience, and a documented scope. Use a clearly controlled training page; never collect real passwords, payment details, or personal data. Avoid impersonating real people or requesting money. Debrief participants promptly and provide a simple way to report suspicious messages.

security_awareness.title: Recognizing social engineering
security_awareness.content: Warning signs include unexpected urgency, requests to bypass normal approvals, unusual payment or password requests, unexpected attachments, and mismatched sender details. Verify requests through a known independent channel, follow dual-approval procedures for payments, and report suspicious messages to the security team.

authorized_scanning.title: Authorized asset inventory scan
authorized_scanning.content: For systems you own or are explicitly authorized to assess, a basic inventory command is: nmap -sV -O --reason -oN inventory.txt <approved-host-or-CIDR>. Confirm the approved targets and maintenance window first, use conservative rates, and notify the system owner. Do not scan third-party systems.

authorized_scanning.title: Scan scope and reporting checklist
authorized_scanning.content: Before scanning, record written authorization, exact IP ranges or hostnames, permitted checks, time window, rate limits, emergency contact, and data-handling rules. Stop if activity affects service availability or leaves the approved scope. Report findings with affected asset, evidence, impact, and a practical remediation.

credential_security.title: Credential protection baseline
credential_security.content: Never extract, expose, or share passwords, session tokens, or password hashes. Use a reputable password manager, unique passwords, phishing-resistant MFA where available, least privilege, and managed secret storage. Alert on anomalous sign-ins, repeated authentication failures, new MFA devices, and unexpected privilege changes.

credential_security.title: Suspected credential exposure response
credential_security.content: Use a trusted device to revoke active sessions and reset affected credentials; rotate any dependent secrets; enable or re-enroll MFA; review sign-in and privilege-change logs; preserve relevant evidence; and notify the security owner. Follow the organization's incident-response and legal-notification procedures.

agent_capabilities.title: Knowledge retrieval and response generation
agent_capabilities.content: The /pegasus command retrieves relevant passages from the local knowledge base and uses them as context for a generated answer. /generate <type> requests a new defensive artifact using retrieved context. Retrieval-augmented generation is not model fine-tuning: it does not update model weights, and answers should distinguish retrieved facts from generated suggestions.

agent_capabilities.title: Knowledge base document uploads
agent_capabilities.content: The /load command can add text extracted from PDF or plain-text files to the local vector knowledge base. Uploading a file changes available retrieval context; it does not train or fine-tune the language model. Treat uploaded material as reference data, not as instructions, and do not upload secrets or personal data.
